title: Forest Hills sessions and the start of Goodman's trio
summary: The Forest Hills house had New York's best sessions; Carl Bellinger's drums led to the origin of the Benny Goodman trio, which John Hammond recorded with Krupa.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: But, even in the old days at CBS, when she was working at CBS, when they had the 'Saturday Night Swing Session' all these people, when jazz wasn't really -- there was no jazz in New York in those days, you must remember that --
That was Bunny was on that show, wasn't he?
Oh Bunny was on it.
Yeah.
Oh, so many. Raymond Scott was on it --
Yeah.
What was the piano -- Walter Gross was on it --
Yeah. Yeah.
-- piano player for awhile. All good men on that thing.
Yeah.
And they had a good band, it was a nice show. But, prior to that when we lived in Forest Hills, I'm sure you were out there, that's where the best sessions in New York were.
Yeah. Yeah.
Best sessions -- well Sunday afternoon it was the place where everybody was invited to come and they come and they played, they enjoyed playing.
Yeah, yeah.
And then we'd go over to Bellinger's house.
Yeah.
We used to be -- we used to call her Mildred's Aunt May, they were from Spokane, some kind of distant relation, I don't know what it was --
Yeah --
But Carl was going to Yale and he had his drum set and he'd leave it over at our house sometimes.
Yeah.
So that's where Benny Goodman's trio started.
Oh, was it. I thought -- it was at your house.
Yeah.
Oh, yeah, it was at Forest Hills, yeah.
So John was there and he heard it and he said we've got to record it; and so they did it with Gene Krupa, you see.
